In all this section we will assume, as in Theorem \ref{th: XX0 XX equality}, that the operators $H_0$ and $A$ satisfy the set of assumptions (A), $H = H_0 + A$, and $\fctshortdef{B}{t \in \setclosure I}{B(t)}$ is a strongly continuous family of bounded self-adjoint operators on $\HHilb$.

issues.failure_explanation: Throughout Section 3.3 the operator S^* includes B(t), and u^* is the solution of the equation with L = B. But E^*(u) contains only the term ∫ e^{-i(t-s)H_0} A u(s) ds, and the proof asserts u − (S_0^*)^{-1}Au = (S_0^*)^{-1}S^*u, which holds only if S^* = S_0^* + A, i.e. B = 0. For B ≠ 0 the unique zero of E^* is the solution of (i∂_t − H)ũ = f, ũ(0)=u_0, which differs from u^*, so the lower bound α(1+T)^{-2}||u−u^*|| ≤ √E^*(u) fails at u = ũ. The corollary as stated is therefore false for B ≠ 0 (or, read charitably, only proved for B = 0 while the section's standing assumptions allow B ≠ 0).
